Clear about your data

Your file stays with you.

TidySheet processes spreadsheets in a background worker inside your browser. The application does not send spreadsheet contents to a server, use analytics, or save your data in browser storage.

What is stored

Imported rows, cleaning settings, manual corrections, and results are held in this tab's memory. Refreshing or closing the page clears them. Downloaded files are saved wherever your browser normally saves downloads.

Hosting and third-party code

The hosting provider receives normal page requests, including connection information such as your IP address. Access to a privately hosted site may require the hosting provider's sign-in. That is separate from spreadsheet processing. The Excel parser is bundled with the app; importing files does not contact a third-party CDN.

What the cleaner changes

You choose the column types and cleaning rules. Date parsing uses the selected day-first or month-first order for numeric dates, and requires four-digit years. Kenyan mobile validation checks the +254 format for numbers beginning with 1 or 7 after the country code; it does not verify allocation, ownership, or activity. Email validation checks common address syntax, not delivery.

Review before use

Invalid values are preserved unless you explicitly choose to drop invalid rows. Duplicate removal keeps the first matching row; it does not merge records. Blank or invalid selected keys never cause rows to be deduplicated. The change log includes standardizations, manual corrections, invalid values, duplicates, and empty rows removed, with source row numbers.

Exports and workbook limits

Each input may be up to 20 MB. Each selected sheet may contain up to 100,000 data rows, 100 columns, and 1,000,000 cells. The cleaner creates a new file of tabular values from one selected worksheet. Styles, macros, and formulas are not retained. Recalculate and save formula workbooks before importing, because only their saved cell results are read.

Excel exports store text as text and supported amounts with up to 15 digits as numeric cells. Longer numbers remain text to avoid precision loss. CSV exports add a leading apostrophe to formula-like text, including +254 mobile numbers, to reduce formula execution risks in spreadsheet software. Use Excel export to retain phone strings without this CSV prefix.

Open-source component

Excel support uses SheetJS Community Edition 0.20.3, distributed under the Apache 2.0 license.
